long_biography.plain_text:
Bill Wirtz helped replace the Chicago Blackhawks' ageing home with the United Center, developed with Chicago Bulls owner Jerry Reinsdorf. The arena opened in 1994 and provided a new venue for both teams. Although Chicago Stadium had long belonged to his family, Wirtz backed its replacement to keep the sports business competitive.

His influence also reached international hockey. When other NHL owners opposed releasing players for the 1972 Summit Series between Canada and the Soviet Union, he argued for participation. Hockey agent Alan Eagleson had promoted the idea; Wirtz helped secure the owners' agreement, allowing leading professionals to represent Canada.
